A protocol for granting a client scoped access to protected resources·After a user approves, an OAuth access token lets a client access a protected resource within its granted scope; the token itself is not generic proof of identity. files.example.com · Authorization

Allow Photo Organizer to view your albums?

Scope: read albums　　Not allowed: delete photos

User approves · returns a scoped access token

OAuth lets a user authorize a client to access a protected resource within a scope. An access token is an access credential, not generic proof of user identity.

What the client receives after OAuth authorization

Jump to the third party to confirm: Clicking sign in with WeChat jumps to WeChat's authorization page; the user approves on a platform they know.

Return with the result: After approval you return to the site with an authorization result; the whole flow never touches the user's WeChat password.

The site still identifies the user: The site uses its own user records to recognize who this is; OAuth grants resource access; it is not authentication and does not replace the site's account system.

What it does not guarantee

OAuth is not a sign-in identity protocol. For provider sign-in, confirm the provider identity mechanism and map it to the site user; provide another sign-in path if the product requires it when authorization is revoked or the provider is unavailable.
